supersedes: e4b-1775-r3 (recorded 2026-07-28 on commit b53b1627, before ADR-064's resident-prompt reduction and #1800 landed — #1764 explicitly identifies that figure as unusable as a regression reference for the system as it now exists)
note: Recorded after ADR-064's resident-prompt reduction (#1827) and #1800 (create_schema description-inference deletion) landed, on a purged DB with a daemon rebuilt from this commit, preflight passing, and guidance provenance verified (5 agent-guidance nodes, 8 skills, versions recorded in provenance.guidance below and identical across all three runs). This results file records run 2 of three (9/12); all three are 6/12, 9/12, 8/12 — mean 7.7/12 (~64%), consistent with this suite's previously-documented variance band. Read the per-scenario traces and the .trace.jsonl raw-output file, not the headline count — see caveats. Working tree was dirty at recording time (the #1764 diagnostic-harness changes themselves, already pushed in this same PR); evalCommit predates one purely cosmetic rename (seed_prompt_nodes -> seed_agent_guidance_nodes, no behavior change) that landed after this run.
caveats: Run-to-run variance is real and substantial: 6/12, 9/12, 8/12 across three consecutive runs with identical guidance and no code changes between them. A single run's count is not a usable signal on its own; this is exactly the noise floor #1764 exists to make visible rather than hide.

Scenario 6 (Update via indirect reference) FAILED in all three runs — the only scenario to do so consistently — but NOT for the same reason each time. Runs 2 and 3 show a clean, repeated pattern: the model asks for a node ID/URI ('I need a specific node ID...', 'Could you provide that node's URI?') instead of calling resolve_query, even though resolve_query is confirmed present in the offered tool list on every one of these turns (verified via the daemon log's 'system prompt and tools prepared' line). Run 1 is a cascade from scenario 4 never creating the node scenario 6 needs, and asks a different, reasonable clarifying question instead. This is a genuine model comprehension gap on the indirect-reference-resolution instruction, not a routing or harness defect — routing succeeded (stage2CandidatesInjected: true) and the tool was offered; the model simply did not reach for it. NOT #1637 (closed, and about resolve_query's return contract once called, which is fixed and confirmed in this code — #1637's own evidence cites 100% success on this exact phrasing when the model DOES call the tool). Tracked by #1835.

create_schema JSON-truncation errors recurred across scenarios 3/8a/8b at varying frequency per run (2/3, 2/3, 2/3 runs respectively). The raw daemon log shows the model emitting genuinely malformed JSON mid-call ('EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 192') on schemas with several fields — a real generation defect on complex nested tool-call arguments, not an argument-shape or prose-contradiction bug (the #1800/coreValues class of defect this suite previously found). The model does not recover with a valid retry within the turn; it reports failure to the user instead.

Checked specifically per #1764's notes: zero occurrences of the 'widget' inert-placeholder leaking into any raw model output or tool call across all three runs (grepped both the .trace.jsonl files and the full daemon log) — the Node Creation skill's placeholder rewrite is holding. Scenarios 4/8c/8d (INSTANCE vs TYPE) passed in 2/3, 3/3, and 1/3 runs respectively; no evidence of a systematic INSTANCE-vs-TYPE comprehension regression from the guidance edit that removed the concrete example, though 8d's variance (2 failures out of 3) is worth watching in a larger future run.

Zero scenarios were excluded as degenerate empty generations in any run (summary.excludedEmptyGenerations: 0 throughout) — every failure above is a genuine scored outcome, not an inference bug misscored as a model failure. The uniformity guard did not fire on any run (all three are comfortably inside the 4-scenario floor and none were uniform pass/fail), which is itself a data point: nothing here looks like a harness artifact.

The routing eval (bun run eval:routing) was also run twice in this same session: 10/15 both times, with an IDENTICAL failure set both runs (indirect-schema-money-owed, ambiguous-client-contacts, out-of-scope-weather, clarification-then-fallthrough, mutating-gate-borderline-schema) — not committed as a separate results file in this PR, but the consistency across two independent runs suggests these are systematic rather than noise, and several read as possible scoring-heuristic gaps rather than model failures (e.g. ambiguous-client-contacts's reply lists disambiguating options in prose but doesn't match isClarification's keyword heuristic) worth a follow-up look rather than a guidance change.
